subject.title: [OAuth] Client ID revoked `app_EMoamEEZ73f0CkXaXp7hrann` - fresh ChatGPT Plus logins completely broken

question: Should OpenClaw keep the upstream Codex OAuth client ID until a real browser invalid-client repro is confirmed, or coordinate a client rotation/override now?
rationale: OAuth app registration and client ownership sit outside a safe autonomous code edit, and the same ID is still used by upstream Codex while OpenClaw's device-code endpoint probe accepts it.

options.title: Verify Then Rotate In Lockstep
options.body: Reproduce the browser failure with a real eligible account, confirm the upstream Codex client/app direction, then update or add an official override consistently across browser, device-code, refresh, and docs.

options.title: Keep Current ID With Fallback Guidance
options.body: If browser invalid-client cannot be confirmed and device-code remains valid, keep the current client ID and improve in-product guidance toward device-code or API-key auth.

options.title: Declare External Until Upstream Changes
options.body: Treat the requested new OAuth app registration as outside OpenClaw until OpenAI/Codex publishes or approves a replacement client path.

recommendation.title: Verify Then Rotate In Lockstep
recommendation.body: Reproduce the browser failure with a real eligible account, confirm the upstream Codex client/app direction, then update or add an official override consistently across browser, device-code, refresh, and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice depends on the OpenAI provider identity and OAuth boundary introduced through the current OpenAI plugin refactor.
